'''Patrick Brosnan''' is an American [[mathematician]], known for his work on [[Motive (algebraic geometry)|motives]], [[Hodge theory]], and [[algebraic groups]]. He received his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1998 under the direction of [[Spencer Bloch]].  Brosnan is the 2009 recipient of the [[Coxeter–James Prize]] of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.math.ca/MediaReleases/2009/res-prizes |title=Press release of the Canadian Mathematical Society |access-date=2009-04-26 |archive-date=2012-11-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102120216/http://math.ca/MediaReleases/2009/res-prizes |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2003, Brosnan (in joint work with [[Prakash Belkale]]) disproved the ''Spanning Tree Conjecture'' of [[Maxim Kontsevich]].<ref>Review of ''Matroids, motives, and a conjecture of Kontsevich'' {{MR|1950482}}</ref>
